note: The routing table as DATA, not code. A table compiled into the guards goes stale the moment a lineup changes, and it goes stale silently — the guards keep running and simply stop classifying correctly. Override without waiting for a release by writing a file of this shape to ~/.claude/agent-companion/state/model-tiers.json (a legacy copy at $CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA/model-tiers.json is still honoured as a fallback); it merges by key, so you can change one model, one effort, or one weight row without restating the rest.

aliasResolution.note: Below v2.1.280, `opus` resolved to Opus 5 instead of Opus 5.5 on the Anthropic API. Every `resolvesTo` block below is only correct on v2.1.280+. Aliases cannot be pinned — they always track the provider's current recommended version; pin with a full model id (e.g. claude-opus-5-5) or an ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_*_MODEL env var instead.

haiku.effortsNote: Haiku 4.5 takes no effort parameter. Setting one on a haiku agent is at best a no-op — the model has one mode, and asking for more thinking does not get any.
haiku.retirementNote: Anthropic: Haiku 4.5 retires no sooner than 2026-10-15. The entire weight 1-2 tier rides on this alias. No successor Haiku has been announced (checked live 2026-09-23). Decide the replacement BEFORE the alias resolves to nothing — the scout raises model_retirement_approaching inside the warning window (now 30 days, not just fixed milestones — see scripts/detect.mjs).

replacement.note: Pre-staged 2026-09-04, re-verified 2026-09-23: still no successor Haiku announced. Sonnet 5 at low effort is the cheapest available tier that takes weight 1-2 work, at roughly 2x Haiku per token (Sonnet 5 $2/$10 vs Haiku 4.5 $1/$5). When a new Haiku ships, add its tier and point this at it - the switch is data, not code. This IS the weight 1-2 fallback if haiku disappears before a successor ships.

sonnet.note: bounded edits, short scripts, multi-file work

opus.effortWarning: Opus 5.5's OWN API default is MEDIUM effort — one level below Opus 5's old HIGH default (checked live 2026-09-23, https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/effort) — but that default is reached only for a bare API call outside any Claude Code session. CORRECTED 2026-09-23 (effort-versions.md research): a Claude Code subagent DEFINITION with no `effort` frontmatter does NOT fall back to this model default; per code.claude.com/docs/en/sub-agents it INHERITS the orchestrating session's current effort. Every effort-taking model has this hazard, not just opus — state effort explicitly rather than relying on inheritance; spawn-guard.mjs warns and the agent-defs audit check flags any definition with a model but no effort, opus included.

fable.effortsNote: Thinking is always on; effort is the only depth control.
fable.note: not a routing tier — an exception requiring a stated warrant
fable.warrantCriterion: Anthropic's own escalation criterion (choosing-a-model, checked live 2026-09-23): 'Use Claude Fable 5.1 ... when your evals on Claude Opus 5.5 at higher effort still fall short.' Fable is now 2.5x Opus on input/output price ($10/$50 vs Opus 5.5's $4/$20 — it was 2x when Opus priced at $5/$25), which strengthens the exception: the warrant is not 'this task is hard', it is 'Opus 5.5 at higher effort was demonstrably tried and fell short'.
behaviorNotes: OFFICIAL (whats-new-fable-5-1): prefers whole-file rewrites, fewer progress updates, less parallel tool batching. Whole-file rewrites make it a poor fit for scoped or mechanical edits even when a warrant exists.

OFFICIAL (whats-new-fable-5-1): same $10/$50 as Fable 5; cache reads at a quarter of the cost ($0.25/MTok, re-verified live 2026-09-23). A long session with a stable prefix is cheaper than sticker price implies - verify the number before relying on it.

COMMUNITY, first-hand (Every.to, TheNeuronDaily): "sticks to what you tell it" is CONTESTED. Reports of overshooting explicit limits (1,000 words -> 1,288; 8-12 quotes -> 43, 5 fabricated) and unprompted style decisions. The friction is over-inference, not literalism. Do not route on an adherence claim.

COMMUNITY, first-hand (dev.to): the gap over Opus/Sonnet is procedural discipline, not intelligence - stating a hypothesis before editing, labelling claims VERIFIED/REASONED/ASSUMED. A brief that carries that checklist closes most of the gap on a cheaper tier, which is exactly what the warrant is meant to make you ask.

mythos.note: same tier and treatment as fable, but not available on this account — kept so it classifies correctly if access ever changes

resolvesTo.note: Not reachable on this account, so pricing/specs are UNVERIFIED — not fetched live. Fill in from the live docs the day access changes rather than guessing now.

opus-5.thinking: adaptive by default (unlike 4.8/4.7); can disable only at <= high, 400 error at xhigh/max
opus-5.note: Superseded by Opus 5.5. The `opus` alias resolved here on Claude Code < v2.1.280 — kept as a reference entry so an agent definition pinned to the dated id (not the alias) still classifies correctly and its effort is validated against what THIS model actually supports, not the current `opus` tier's list.

fable-5.note: Superseded by Fable 5.1. Cache-hit pricing is the 0.1x rate, NOT Fable 5.1's 0.025x rate — do not reuse 5.1's cache economics for a definition pinned to this id.

opus-4-8.thinking: adaptive is the ONLY on-mode; omitting `thinking` entirely runs WITHOUT thinking - must be set explicitly. xhigh recommended for coding/agentic use.
opus-4-8.note: Not validated by this table's effort checks for the thinking-omission hazard (agent definition frontmatter here carries no `thinking` field to check) - flagged in docs/proposed/global-doctrine-reweight.patch as a known gap, not silently assumed safe.

opus-4-7.thinking: same as 4.8 - adaptive is the only on-mode; omitting `thinking` runs WITHOUT it. xhigh recommended.

opus-4-6.thinking: adaptive recommended; budget_tokens still functional as a transitional escape hatch
opus-4-6.note: NO xhigh — this generation stops at max/high/medium/low. An agent definition pinned to this id with effort: xhigh is invalid on this model, not just 'more than needed'; validated via referenceModels, not the current opus tier's effort list.

sonnet-4-6.thinking: adaptive recommended (medium recommended default in practice); budget_tokens still functional
sonnet-4-6.note: NO xhigh, same as opus-4-6 — validated against this list, not the current sonnet tier's (which does have xhigh).

referenceModelsNote: Non-routable reference entries for OLDER pinned model ids, so an agent definition pinned to a full/dated id (not an alias) is classified as premium/non-premium correctly by classifyModel() (unchanged — these ids already match the current alias tier's regex loosely) AND has its EFFORT validated against what that specific model actually supports via classifyReferenceModel()/referenceEffortSupported() in hooks/lib/context.mjs, rather than against the current alias tier's (possibly wider) effort list. Source: live-docs.md §1, fetched 2026-09-23. Not part of `routing` — nothing routes here, they exist only for validation of an id someone already pinned.
availabilityNote: An entry with available:false is still classified, but an agent definition pinned to it is a finding. A model you cannot reach fails at spawn time with nothing having warned you beforehand, and the failure surfaces as a broken agent rather than as a configuration mistake. Set available:false for anything outside your plan.
unknownNote: A model matching no entry is treated as PREMIUM and flagged. Defaulting an unrecognised model to cheap would let a new top-tier model bypass the warrant and the cap on the day it ships — the exact window in which nobody has updated the table yet. Fail toward the expensive assumption; the cost of a spurious warrant is one line in a brief.

low.note: skip thinking; reads and single commands

xhigh.note: recommended start for agentic work on current top tiers

max.note: reserve for genuinely frontier problems; large cost for small gain

effortNote: Ranks are global so two agents on different models stay comparable — the reviewer-parity rule needs that. The supported SET is per-tier, under each entry's "efforts", because availability genuinely differs by model. An effort not in a tier's list is not a smaller amount of thinking; it is a parameter that model does not take.

3.label: moderate — bounded multi-step, parse structured output

routingNote: Task weight 1-5 maps to a model AND an effort. Round DOWN when uncertain and escalate on failure; over-provisioning is a rule violation, not a safety margin. Weight 4 may take opus where blast radius warrants it. Nothing routes to fable — it is an exception, not a row.
ladderNote: The routing grid (weight x kind, floored by consequence) still picks (model, effort) exactly as before — this ladder does not change that logic, it is the ORDERED VIEW of the same (model, effort) pairs, cheapest to dearest, each mapped to a spawnable generic worker definition under agents/ (namespaced <plugin>:<agent> when spawned from outside this repo, e.g. agent-companion:ac-sonnet-medium) because the Agent tool has no per-spawn effort parameter — effort is locked to whichever definition's frontmatter is used. Fable is deliberately NOT a rung: it sits outside the ladder as a warranted exception (see the fable tier's warrantCriterion), never a routine destination. The CURRENT weight defaults (1-2 haiku, 3 sonnet/medium=rung 3, 4 sonnet/high=rung 4, 5 opus/xhigh=rung 9) are UNCHANGED by adding this view — see `routing` and `taskKinds` for what actually picks a rung; a pending research finding may revise those defaults later as a pure data edit, without touching the ladder shape itself. Consequence floors already raise the rung the same way they raise effort/model in effortFor(): `elevated` floors effort at `high` (>= rung 4 within whichever model the weight already picked), `critical` floors the model at opus AND the effort at xhigh (>= rung 9).

mechanical.note: Small answer space with one right shape. More thinking does not produce a better result, it produces the same result more slowly.

examples: a feature against a clear spec
bounded.note: The shape is known; the work is filling it in correctly.

diagnostic.note: A search problem. The answer exists but must be found, and more passes genuinely raise the odds of finding it.

novel-design.note: Large answer space with no known-good shape to copy. Each additional pass tends to surface a failure mode that would otherwise ship.

taskKindNote: Weight sets the MODEL — how much capability the task needs. Kind adjusts the EFFORT — how much the answer benefits from search. They are orthogonal: a routing table and a message bus can touch the same number of files and deserve completely different amounts of thinking. Compute effort as routing[weight].effort shifted by taskKinds[kind].effortDelta, clamped to the efforts table. When the kind is unclear, use bounded and escalate on failure rather than pre-paying for search you may not need.

reviewerParity.note: A reviewer is sized to the writer it gates. The MODEL must match: a weaker reviewer catches the errors it would itself have avoided and waves through the ones it would itself have made, which is the novel-error class a stronger writer produces. EFFORT may go higher and must not go lower — refutation is a search problem and can need more thinking than generation did.

elevated.note: A mistake here costs other people time but is recoverable.

critical.note: A mistake here is expensive or irreversible.

consequenceNote: Consequence is a FLOOR, not a delta, and it is applied AFTER the kind adjustment so it cannot be undercut. This matters because difficulty and consequence are close to orthogonal: a one-line production migration is mechanical by KIND, which would otherwise push its effort DOWN on precisely the change most likely to hurt. The floor is the answer to "how bad is it if this is wrong", which is a different question from "how hard is this to get right".

explore.summary: read-only search: where is X, what touches Y, does Z exist
explore.provenance: OFFICIAL choosing-a-model: Haiku for subagent tasks. COMMUNITY consensus: haiku, cost-driven.

mechanical-edit.summary: rename, config edit, reformat, apply a known migration recipe
mechanical-edit.provenance: COMMUNITY (Wavect): avoid Fable for tiny fixes, CRUD, renaming, formatting, boilerplate.

bounded-feature.summary: a feature against a clear spec, 1-3 files, known shape
bounded-feature.provenance: OFFICIAL choosing-a-model: Sonnet for everyday code generation and agentic tool use. COMMUNITY: Sonnet 5 delivers near-Opus coding at Sonnet price; escalate to Opus when the spec is incomplete or moves mid-run.

integration.summary: multi-file, cross-referencing, touches shared config or things other agents depend on
integration.provenance: Our weight scale. Consequence elevated because shared surfaces are where a mistake costs other people time.

debug-root-cause.summary: a specific failure, unexplained regression, flaky test - the answer exists and must be found
debug-root-cause.provenance: COMMUNITY: Sonnet 5 praised first-hand for tracing brownfield failures to root causes rather than patching symptoms. Escalate to Opus when evidence conflicts or constraints are hidden.

large-refactor.summary: large-scale refactor across a module or subsystem; the target shape is known, the surface is wide
large-refactor.provenance: OFFICIAL choosing-a-model: Opus for large-scale refactoring and complex systems engineering.

novel-design.summary: a protocol, concurrency or sync/merge logic, a message bus, a new abstraction with no known-good shape
novel-design.provenance: Our kind axis. OFFICIAL: Opus for complex systems engineering. Fable only with a warrant - and per the procedural-discipline finding, first try a brief that carries the verification checklist on Opus.

critical-change.summary: production data, migrations, destructive ops, auth, billing, secrets - regardless of size
critical-change.provenance: Consequence axis (arXiv 2606.04402: consequence is orthogonal to difficulty). The floor raises even a one-line change to opus/xhigh.

code-review.summary: adversarial review of a diff; sized to the writer it gates
code-review.provenance: Our reviewer-parity rule. BENCHMARK (CodeRabbit, semi-vendor): review precision tops out ~37% across every model tested and no model wins both precision and recall - so tier choice does not make review sufficient; adversarial framing and a human gate on critical changes still matter. CAVEAT under calibration: one first-hand report (Wavect) found HIGH effort slower AND lower-recall than LOW on review. See calibration.

long-autonomous-run.summary: an agent session expected to run for hours with minimal supervision
long-autonomous-run.provenance: OFFICIAL choosing-a-model: Fable for agent sessions that run for hours. COMMUNITY, first-hand (TheNeuronDaily): management overhead from unrequested inferences grows with autonomy. Warrant required for Fable; Opus/xhigh is the default.

subagent-worker.summary: a delegated worker doing a bounded, well-specified piece of a larger task
subagent-worker.provenance: OFFICIAL choosing-a-model: Haiku for subagent tasks. Raise the weight if the piece is not actually bounded.

verify.summary: confirm a claim against reality: read a file, check a value, take a screenshot, does X exist/match Y — reports back, changes nothing
verify.provenance: Calibration finding 'haiku validates, it does not OPERATE' (team-orchestration skill; CONTRIBUTIONS_INBOX @ 9b355e7). The defining trait is that nothing changes: the task ends when the answer is read back, not when a step is performed.

operate.summary: execute an ordered procedure or change a live system — even when every individual step looks trivial in isolation
operate.provenance: Calibration finding 'haiku validates, it does not OPERATE' (team-orchestration skill; CONTRIBUTIONS_INBOX @ 9b355e7). A sequence of trivial-looking steps against a live system is not a verify task: ordering mistakes, partial failures, and side effects compound in a way a single read-only check cannot, so this floors at sonnet even though no one step looks hard. Raise weight/consequence further when a step is itself destructive, production-facing, or irreversible (critical-change already covers that).

taskTypesNote: A task type is a named preset over (weight, kind, consequence). Resolve it through the same grid as everything else; do not special-case it. "parity" as a weight means: match the writer being reviewed. "inherit" as a consequence means: take the consequence of the change under review. Provenance is recorded per entry because these WILL go stale - the scout re-checks the lineup, and a routing review should re-read the sources, not the table.

reviewer-effort-direction.question: Does a reviewer at HIGHER effort than the writer catch more, or less?
reviewer-effort-direction.tension: Our rule says effort may exceed and must not drop. One first-hand report (Wavect) found high-effort review slower and lower-recall than low. Willison observed that past high, Fable drafts the deliverable in thinking and rewrites it - double cost, no gain.
reviewer-effort-direction.measure: From telemetry: for reviews, compare findings-per-review and post-merge defect rate by reviewer effort relative to writer effort. Needs reviewers to report findings structurally.

fable-cache-economics.question: Does Fable 5.1 cache-read pricing make long stable-prefix sessions competitive with Opus?
fable-cache-economics.tension: Official: cache reads at a quarter of the cost ($0.25/MTok). Our measured cache hit ratio is ~96%. Fable is now 2.5x Opus on sticker price (was 2x, before Opus 5.5 dropped to $4/$20) - the cache discount has a wider gap to close than it did. At max effort output tokens run ~1.7x Fable 5 - the discount may be eaten by verbosity.
fable-cache-economics.measure: From telemetry: per-session cost by model with cache-read share. Compare fable vs opus on sessions of similar turn count.

sonnet-vs-opus-at-weight-5.question: Is Sonnet 5 sufficient for some weight-5 work?
sonnet-vs-opus-at-weight-5.tension: Vendor benchmarks put Sonnet 5 above Opus 5 on Terminal-Bench 2.1 and some agentic evals at ~40% less cost. Vendor-run, and an outlier.
sonnet-vs-opus-at-weight-5.measure: From telemetry: escalation rate (a Sonnet spawn re-run at Opus) by task type. If weight-5 bounded work rarely escalates from Sonnet, lower the base.

procedural-checklist-vs-tier.question: Does a verification checklist in the brief substitute for a higher tier?
procedural-checklist-vs-tier.tension: First-hand: teaching Opus/Sonnet the Fable-style checklist (hypothesis before edit, VERIFIED/REASONED/ASSUMED labels) closes most of the gap. If true, many Fable warrants should be declined in favour of a better brief.
procedural-checklist-vs-tier.measure: From telemetry: warrant acceptance rate, and outcome of warranted Fable spawns vs Opus spawns with a checklist brief on the same task type.
